name: Question 10
problem:
Find $f(0)$ given that  $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are two continuous vector-valued functions for which   $g(0)=⟨-1,0,1⟩$ and 

$$
{lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)-g(t)]=⟨-2,-3,0⟩\,.
$$
worked_solution:
Using the  addition rule for limits, and the fact that both functions are continuous, we get:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)-g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)+{lim}_{t\to 0}[-g(t)] \\  & ={lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)-{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) \\  & =f(0)-g(0) \\  & =f(0)-{{⟨-1,0,1⟩}_{⏟}}_{g(0)}\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, we are told that:

$$
{lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)-g(t)]=⟨-2,-3,0⟩
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain the following equation which we can solve for $f(0):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)-g(t)] & =⟨-2,-3,0⟩ \\ ⟨-2,-3,0⟩ & =f(0)-⟨-1,0,1⟩ \\ ⟨-2,-3,0⟩+⟨-1,0,1⟩ & =f(0) \\ f(0) & =⟨-3,-3,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

a
⟨−1,−3,−1⟩
b
⟨1,3,1⟩

⟨0,−3,1⟩
d
⟨−3,−3,1⟩
e
The value of f(0) cannot be determined.

Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the addition rule for limits, and the fact that both functions are continuous, we get:

limt→0[f(t)−g(t)]=limt→0f(t)+limt→0[−g(t)]=limt→0f(t)−limt→0g(t)=f(0)−g(0)=f(0)−⟨−1,0,1⟩⏟g(0)

On the other hand, we are told that: limt→0[f(t)−g(t)]=⟨−2,−3,0⟩

Therefore, we obtain the following equation which we can solve for f(0):

limt→0[f(t)−g(t)]=⟨−2,−3,0⟩⟨−2,−3,0⟩=f(0)−⟨−1,0,1⟩⟨−2,−3,0⟩+⟨−1,0,1⟩=f(0)f(0)=⟨−3,−3,1⟩
